description: Cellular and compartmentalised. Living bright bedrooms dim. Deep — views through multiple spaces. Clear functional corridor connecting zones. Kitchen: L-shaped or U-shaped, no island or peninsula — counter set back from windows, moderate natural light. Cook faces the wall — back to the living and dining area. Two cooks can work simultaneously on separate counter runs. Fully open plan — no wall separates kitchen from dining and living. Living arrangement: split seating-kitchen-dining, kitchen on side wall. Seating: An L-shaped sofa in the upper-left living area facing inward toward the room; a second seating block near the centre facing the TV area. Dining table (6 seats). TV on wall left of entry. Cook may see TV from cooking position. Diners do not face the TV. Entry: corridor entry, first thing visible on arrival is bedroom doors, L-shaped corridor, medium length. No door between entry and living — relevant where local regulations require separation. Master suite (en-suite bathroom) — accessed via own door off corridor, no walk-in wardrobe. Master suite (en-suite bathroom) at the rear — maximum distance from entry, best acoustic separation from living activity. Secondary bedroom 1 — accessed via own door off corridor, desk visible. Secondary bedroom 2 — accessed via own door off corridor, desk visible. Each single bedroom can function as a dedicated home office, hobby room, guest room, or children's bedroom. 2 of 2 have a desk visible in plan. Single bedroom use options: children's bedroom / dedicated home office / hobby or creative studio / guest room / home office + children's bedroom simultaneously. Storage: generous wardrobe storage. Sanitary rooms: bathroom (shower and toilet); bathroom (shower, bathtub, and toilet). Two bathrooms — two people can shower simultaneously, parallel morning and evening routines possible. Suits: families with two or more children; multi-generational households. Not suitable for: households needing a master suite with walk-in wardrobe storage; people who want bedrooms with strong natural light, as the central bedrooms appear dim and deep in the plan; wheelchair users, given the L-shaped corridor and tight compartmentalised rooms.
